title: Deployment & Final Checklist
description: Deploy the blog to Vercel, set up CI/CD, monitor performance, and ensure everything is production‑ready.

slides.title: Ready for the World 🌍
slides.content:
# Time to Deploy!

We'll use Vercel because it provides:

* Zero‑config Next.js deployment.
* Automatic SSL and CDN.
* Preview deployments for PRs.
* Analytics and Core Web Vitals.

But the same principles apply to Docker, AWS, or any Node.js host.

slides.title: Step 1: Push to GitHub & Import to Vercel 🔄
slides.content:
# Deployment Steps

1. Make sure all env vars are set in Vercel dashboard (or via CLI).
2. Connect your GitHub repository.
3. Vercel detects Next.js; simply click Deploy.
4. After deployment, set your custom domain.

Your blog is live!

slides.title: Vercel CLI Deployment (optional)
slides.content: You can also deploy from the terminal.

slides.title: Step 2: Environment Variables 🔑
slides.content:
# Secrets in Production

In Vercel dashboard (or via `vercel env add`), add:

* `DATABASE_URL` – if using PostgreSQL (on Vercel, you might use `vercel-postgres`).
* `GITHUB_ID` & `GITHUB_SECRET` – OAuth credentials.
* `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` – strong random string.
* `NEXTAUTH_URL` – `https://yourdomain.com`.

**Important:** For SQLite, Vercel's serverless environment has a read‑only filesystem. You must switch to a hosted database (like PlanetScale, Supabase, or Vercel Postgres) for production.

quizData.question: Why can't you use SQLite in production on Vercel?

options.text: SQLite is not supported by Next.js
Vercel's serverless functions have an ephemeral, read‑only filesystem that resets
SQLite is too slow for production
Prisma doesn't support SQLite in production

quizData.explanation: Vercel uses serverless functions with a temporary filesystem. Any file written (like the SQLite DB) is lost and cannot be shared across instances.

slides.title: Step 3: CI/CD & Monitoring 🧪
slides.content:
# Automate & Observe

* **Preview Deployments**: Every PR creates a unique URL; test changes before merging.
* **Branch Protection**: Set up rules to require passing builds before merging.
* **Vercel Analytics**: Monitor Core Web Vitals, page views, and error rates.
* **Logs**: Check runtime and build logs to debug issues.

You can also integrate Sentry for error tracking.

slides.title: Final Production Checklist ✅
slides.content:
# Before You Go Live

- [ ] Environment variables set correctly.
- [ ] Database migrated and seeded.
- [ ] Authentication callback URL points to production.
- [ ] Custom 404 and error pages in place.
- [ ] Images served from a whitelisted domain.
- [ ] `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` generated (next‑sitemap).
- [ ] Analytics/tracking added (optional).
- [ ] Test all flows: sign in, add comment, create post.

Once checked, your blog is ready for the world!

slides.title: Sitemap Generation (next-sitemap.config.js)
slides.content: Automatically create a sitemap for SEO.

quizData.question: What does `next-sitemap` do?

options.text: Generates a dynamic sitemap.xml and robots.txt for better search engine crawling
Creates a sitemap of component dependencies

quizData.explanation: `next-sitemap` is a popular package that scans your Next.js pages and generates a sitemap to submit to search engines.

slides.title: Congratulations 🎉
slides.content: You have built a full‑stack, production‑ready blog with Next.js! From routing to database, authentication to deployment, you now possess the skills to bring any web application idea to life. Keep building, keep learning!
